chunks: When they have reached their appointed time, then either keep them lawfully or let them go honourably; but have two witnesses from among you, and give truthful evidence for (being acceptable to) God. This is to warn him who believes in God and the Last Day. God will furnish a way out for him who fears Him,
ai.seo_question: What are the proper procedures and ethical guidelines for divorce in Islam according to the Quran?
ai.summary: This verse, the final in Surah At-Talaq, establishes the legal framework for divorce by mandating retention or release with kindness during the 'Iddah period, witnessed by just men. In Shia jurisprudence, the requirement of 'just witnesses' (Dhawu 'Adl) underscores the communal verification of marital status, while the concluding promise of a 'way out' (Makhraj) for the God-conscious highlights the spiritual reward for adhering to these divine protocols with sincerity.
